evals.prompt: We need a new follower behavior: when the host signals a re-anchor mid-playback, the follower should, instead of a hard seek, do a soft nudge to the expected position and log a 'reconciled' telemetry event. Add this.
evals.expected_output: The new lifecycle behavior belongs in syncReducer (pure, no React/player/network), not the React controller. Add a new SyncEvent/SyncEffect variant + a transition test in watch-sync-machine.test.ts. The reducer decides which effect class (the soft nudge); sync-math.ts computes the numbers (kept side-effect-free). Telemetry is derived via syncTelemetryEvents(prev, event, next), not hand-placed track() calls. Side effects only run in use-sync-controller.ts via returned effects. selectSyncStatus 3-value contract unchanged.
expectations: The new lifecycle behavior is added as a new SyncEvent/SyncEffect variant in syncReducer (sync-machine.ts), not as a branch in the React controller (use-sync-controller.ts)
A transition test is added in watch-sync-machine.test.ts covering the new event/effect variant
syncReducer and sync-math.ts helpers stay pure (no React, no player, no network access; no mutation of input state)
Telemetry is emitted via syncTelemetryEvents(prev, event, next), not via ad-hoc track() calls in the controller
The selectSyncStatus 3-value public contract is preserved unchanged

evals.prompt: The clock offset estimate jumps around because of network jitter. I'll average the N probe samples in useServerClock to smooth it out — that should stabilize the Cristian estimate.
evals.expected_output: Reject averaging clock samples. Averaging lets high-RTT outliers inflate the half-RTT asymmetry error. useServerClock probes N~3 times per sync and keeps the min-RTT sample via selectBestClockSample to bound the asymmetry error. clockReady gates the sync phase. Averaging is a known failure mode — use selectBestClockSample (min-RTT), do not average.
expectations: Rejects averaging the clock probe samples (cites the known failure mode: sync drifts under variable latency when samples are averaged instead of min-RTT selected)
Recommends using selectBestClockSample to keep the min-RTT sample (Cristian-style), not averaging
Notes that clockReady gates the sync phase

evals.prompt: In use-sync-controller.ts, after a successful nudge I'll add a track('sync.reconciled', {...}) call right where the effect is applied, so product can see reconcile events. It's just one line.
evals.expected_output: Reject ad-hoc track() in the controller. Telemetry must be derived via syncTelemetryEvents(prev, event, next) so it cannot drift from behavior. Scattering track() calls in the controller is a known failure mode: telemetry disagrees with actual transitions. Add the telemetry to the derived secretion path, not a one-off track() in the executor.
expectations: Rejects adding an ad-hoc track() call in use-sync-controller.ts (known failure mode: telemetry disagrees with actual transitions)
Recommends emitting telemetry only via syncTelemetryEvents(prev, event, next) so it is derived, not hand-placed
Notes the observability seam stays a vendor-neutral no-op (no vendor SDK introduced)
